themes_detail.label: SPIT Inspections Surge
themes_detail.summary: Special Projects Inspection Team (SPIT) complaints spiked to 5 this week, a 1233% increase versus the 0.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 9.55), suggesting either a concentrated enforcement action or emerging building/occupancy violations in Bushwick that warrant investigation into what triggered the surge.
evidence: 5 SPIT complaints this week vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 9.55 indicates statistically extreme anomaly
Highest-ranked spike in entire dataset by magnitude and statistical significance
reporting_angles: Interview DOB and SPIT to confirm if targeted enforcement action is underway; if so, what violations prompted it
Canvass affected addresses to understand what residents and landlords are experiencing; are illegal conversions, overcrowding, or code violations driving the uptick?

themes_detail.label: Bus Stop Infrastructure Collapse
themes_detail.summary: Bus stop shelter complaints jumped to 3 this week, a 1100% spike versus the 0.2 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.35), indicating rapid deterioration of transit infrastructure in Bushwick that may reflect deferred MTA maintenance or storm damage.
evidence: 3 bus stop shelter complaints this week vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 6.35 reflects highly significant spike
Second-highest spike in dataset by statistical magnitude
reporting_angles: Contact MTA to identify which shelters are damaged and timeline for repairs; map locations to see if clustered in one area
Photo essay documenting broken shelters and interviewing commuters on how conditions affect their daily transit

themes_detail.label: Unsanitary Conditions Spike
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary condition complaints jumped to 78 last week, a 116% increase versus the 36.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 3.74), pointing to a sudden deterioration in street and building cleanliness across Bushwick that may reflect sanitation collection failures or pest outbreaks.
evidence: 78 unsanitary condition complaints last week vs. 36.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Unsanitary condition also in top-10 volume complaints overall (515 over 90 days)
Z-score of 3.74 indicates statistically significant anomaly
reporting_angles: Contact Sanitation Department to confirm if collection routes were disrupted, staffing shortages, or equipment failures caused the jump
Ground reporting: visit high-complaint blocks to photograph conditions and interview residents about duration and severity of uncollected waste, rat/pest activity

themes_detail.label: Non-Emergency Police Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police matter complaints surged to 15 last week, a 155% increase versus the 5.9 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.04), suggesting heightened street-level disturbances, quality-of-life issues, or crime concerns that warrant understanding what specific incidents are driving calls.
evidence: 15 non-emergency police matter complaints last week vs. 5.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 4.04 reflects statistically significant deviation
Likely correlated with noise spikes: residential noise complaints total 1574 over 90 days
reporting_angles: Review NYPD CompStat data and 311 detail records to categorize the 15 complaints (assault, theft, disorderly conduct, etc.) and identify hotspot locations
Interview NYPD precinct commander and community leaders to assess whether this is localized or district-wide; connect with residents in affected areas

themes_detail.label: Dead/Dying Tree Crisis (2 weeks)
themes_detail.summary: Dead and dying tree complaints hit 4 two weeks ago, a 433% jump versus the 0.8 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.91), suggesting either storm damage, disease, or neglected Parks maintenance that may require rapid intervention to prevent hazards or further ecological decline.
evidence: 4 dead/dying tree complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 4.91 indicates statistically significant spike
Street sign damage also spiked (3 complaints 2 weeks ago, +500%), suggesting possible storm event
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Parks to determine if a specific weather event (high winds, disease) caused die-off; ask about inspection timeline and removal schedule
Map the four locations and photograph conditions; assess whether residents perceive safety or aesthetic concerns
